'''Vincent Lamberti''' (c. 1927/28 – March 21, 2014) was an American chemist and inventor, who held 118 granted patents, and is best known as the inventor of [[Dove soap]].

==Early life==
Vincent Lamberti grew up in [[Meriden, Connecticut]],<ref name=TheRecord>Levin, Jay. [https://web.archive.org/web/20161104225035/http://www.northjersey.com/news/farewell-to-the-father-of-dove-soap-researcher-vincent-lamberti-86-of-upper-saddle-river-dies-1.841570 "Farewell to the father of Dove soap: Researcher Vincent Lamberti, 86, of Upper Saddle River, dies"], ''[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]'', April 4, 2014, backed up by the [[Internet Archive]] as of November 4, 2016. Accessed September 13, 2017.</ref> the youngest son of immigrant parents from [[Avellino]].<ref name=YaleAlumni>[https://www.yalealumnimagazine.com/obituaries/1326 "In Remembrance: Vincent Lamberti '47, '51PhD"]. ''[[Yale Alumni Magazine]]''. April 2014.</ref> He was so advanced academically that according to his son, Vincent James, he substitute-taught his high school physics class when the teacher was absent.<ref name=TheRecord/> While in high school, he met his future wife, Ileana.<ref name=YaleAlumni/> Lamberti won a scholarship to [[Yale University]], where he was thought of as such a "[[geek]]" that his dorm mates were known to lock him out of his room, forcing him to climb up a drain pipe to get back into his dormitory. 
He was a member of [[Phi Beta Kappa Society]] and the [[Sigma Xi]] society. He earned his undergraduate degree in 1947 and earned a doctorate in organic chemistry in 1951.<ref name=TheRecord/><ref name=YaleAlumni/>

==Career==
Lamberti joined [[Lever Brothers]] in 1949 after interviewing with major drug and chemical companies. Lamberti spent 40 years with the company, mostly at its [[Edgewater, New Jersey]] research center, where, as patent coordinator and manager of organic chemistry, he led a team to create new and improved products. In the 1950s, Lamberti developed an easier and relatively inexpensive process to manufacture a synthetic compound to replace the fatty acids in bar soap, which was considered a breakthrough in the development of synthetic bar soap. This led to the [[Dove beauty bar]], which Lever Brothers marketed as being less irritating to the skin than traditional soaps.<ref name=TheRecord/><ref name=YaleAlumni/> Other brands Lamberti helped develop or improve include [[Wisk]] and [[Aim toothpaste]].<ref name=TheRecord/>

Lamberti was an opponent of [[animal testing]], and did not participate in that practice.<ref name=TheRecord/>

Lamberti accumulated a total of 118 granted [[patent]]s, in the U.S. and other countries, all of which were property of Lever Brothers. According to Stephen Madison, senior principal scientist with [[Unilever]], of which Lever Brothers was part (and whom Lamberti hired), no one else at Unilever held as many patents.<ref name=TheRecord/> He also wrote over 2,000 patents for other inventors all over the world.<ref name=YaleAlumni/>

==Personal life==
Lamberti lived in [[Upper Saddle River, New Jersey]]. He died on March 21, 2014, of congestive [[heart failure]], at the age of 86. He was survived by his wife of 64 years, Ileana, their children, Vincent James and Laana Peters, and four grandsons,<ref name=TheRecord/> William, Dylan, Morgan, and Dylan.<ref name=YaleAlumni/>
